# Soumyajit Das — Personal Portfolio

> Physics researcher and scientific software developer. M.Sc. Physics student at NIT Silchar
> specialising in density functional theory (DFT) of 2D materials. Creator of VaspViz and WallPrx.
> This file guides AI agents through the site at https://soumyajit9696.github.io/.

## Profile
- Name: Soumyajit Das
- Role: Physics Researcher & Scientific Software Developer
- Location: Silchar, Assam, India
- Email: dsoumyajit295@gmail.com
- Education: M.Sc. Physics (Applied), NIT Silchar (2024–2026); B.Sc. Physics (Hons), University of Calcutta (2020–2023, CGPA 8.11)
- Research: Density functional theory, transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), optoelectronic properties, condensed matter physics
- Internship: IISER Kolkata, SSPL Lab under Prof. Satyabrata Raj (May–July 2025)

## Projects
- M.Sc. project report: ab-initio DFT study of monolayer and bilayer ZrS2 and ZrSe2 (NIT Silchar, Dept. of Physics, 2026) — leads the Projects page as a featured card: details left, front-page cover right
- Summer internship report: first-principles DFT calculations on crystalline materials with VASP and Elk (IISER Kolkata, Dept. of Physical Sciences, 2025) — second featured card on the Projects page
- VaspViz: cross-platform PyQt6 desktop suite for post-processing VASP output — band structures, DOS, fat bands, Wannier90 overlays, optical spectra, 3D POSCAR viewer, CHGCAR rendering, EOS fitting, convergence monitoring. Python, PyQt6, Matplotlib, NumPy, SciPy. https://github.com/Soumyajit9696/VaspViz
- WallPrx: minimal, ad-free wallpaper discovery platform for high-resolution desktop and mobile wallpapers. HTML, CSS, JavaScript. https://github.com/Soumyajit9696/WallPrx
- Theorem: LaTeX equation editor and image generator (web + desktop). https://sci-tech-science.blogspot.com/2026/10/theorem-latex-equation-editor.html

- [Gallery](https://soumyajit9696.github.io/gallery.html): B.Sc memory, NIT Diary, physics and travel photos

## Interactive features (all pages)
- Tools dock (bottom-right "Tools" button): draggable clock, BibTeX citation, links, feedback (opens mail app)
- Atom Orbiter cursor (desktop only): the pointer is a live atom - nucleus dot at the true pointer, three precessing elliptical orbits on a damped spring (length contraction while moving), electrons whose spin follows the pointer's kinetic energy, a comet particle wake (additive glow in dark mode), excited energy state over links (expanded accent shells + spectrum electrons), cooling idle state, photon rings + particle burst on click. The system sits exactly under the pointer and the native OS cursor is fully hidden. Press Shift+R for a reading guide, Shift+M for an on-screen caliper (px/cm/degrees; status chip + auto-clear after the second point), Esc to clear
- Welcome note: first homepage visit per session shows a greeting card with a time-of-day title (Good morning/afternoon/evening/night, visitor!), a live clock chip and a matching well-wish (dialog with Esc/backdrop close)
